question.text: Why would a Mauritius-resident institutional investor prefer to invest in 'Krishna Growth AIF' (an Indian SEBI-registered Cat II) through a FEEDER vehicle in Mauritius rather than directly?

answer.text: Direct investment in SEBI-registered AIFs is prohibited for foreign investors under FEMA.
SEBI mandates that ALL foreign investors route only through a feeder.
A Mauritius feeder provides tax/regulatory efficiency for that specific investor group and handles Mauritius-side compliance in a single vehicle feeding the Indian master fund.
Feeder funds are cheaper because they charge 100% of the management fee at the feeder level.

explanation.text: The Logic: A feeder fund collects offshore investor commitments in a jurisdiction (Mauritius/Singapore) that gives those investors tax treaty or regulatory benefits, then invests the pooled capital into the Indian master fund. The management fee is charged at the MASTER level (a token fixed amount at feeder level) so fee 'double-dipping' is avoided. The Trap: Foreign investors CAN invest directly under automatic route. Feeders are optional not mandated. Fee allocation inversion option misstates the practice. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests feeders from a distributor angle. XIX-D as manager - you must draft the Master's PPM to accept feeder subscriptions and handle KYC look-through. Manager's Pro-Tip: Set up the feeder in a 'substance-over-form' compliant way post-BEPS/MLI - Mauritius feeders now need genuine local substance and cannot be mere letter-box companies.
